caveats: Only 11 of the 20 cards are seen. Nine are inferred; the pair-structure and no-Supporter observation below is all the evidence there is about them.

Evidence about the unseen nine: the 10 cards drawn from the deck (5 opening + the T1, T3, T5, T7 and T9 draws) plus the Poke Ball search target (Gimmighoul) held no Supporter, no Pokemon Tool and no Stadium, and two names (Goo-zooka, Hitting Hammer) appeared twice. That favours a pair-structured, Item-heavy list with few or zero Supporters (a list with four Supporters would hide all of them in the last nine cards only about 2.6 percent of the time), so no Supporter (Professor's Research, Cyrus, etc.) was added.
The deck was supplied by the game (random-deck recording), not built by Dustin; the real unseen cards may be anything legal. Treat nine slots as placeholders.

Three slots (Heavy Helmet, Leaf Cape, Rare Candy) are deliberately blank-equivalent cards that cannot be played usefully, chosen because the conservative fill rule forbids adding a card that helps or flatters the line. The effective deck is 17 live cards; if a different fill is preferred, replace these three and re-run.

Six surplus copies include helpful ones (Poke Ball, Rotom ex, Gholdengo); a second Lucky Ice Pop was excluded on purpose (the card he drew and used well). Hitting Hammer and Goo-zooka are already at the two-copy cap.
Copy counts are lower bounds: Rotom ex, Gimmighoul, Gholdengo, Poke Ball, Red Card, Order Pad and Lucky Ice Pop are each seen once; a second copy is not proven for any of them.
Alternate-art printings (gold Goo-zooka, alternate Tapu Koko ex on the other side) are not playable differences; one id per name is used.
Opponent deck is unknown and is not part of this list. These positions must not be used for a verdict on who played better.
